title: Seeming clash: same species as dead faith yet dead faith profits nothing
source_text: XLVIII. Videri posset majoris momenti quod communi consensu docent Scholae Romanae Theologi; nempe fidem salvificam atque justificantem non esse quid diversum & specie distinctum ab ista fide mortua & informi; quod etiam non satis concordare videtur cum eo quod jamjam diximus eos fateri atque agnoscere, nimirum fidem mortuam & informem ad salutem nihil prodesse, & ad justitiam esse inutilem. Quomodo enim ista constare possunt, fidem mortuam nihil ad salutem prodesse, & tamen illam esse unicam & eandem cum fide salvifica atque justificante, nec ab ea specie distingui?
pass_a_gloss: It might seem of greater moment that the theologians of the Roman school teach by common consent that saving and justifying faith is not something diverse and specifically distinct from that dead and unformed faith; which also does not seem to agree well enough with what we have just said they admit and acknowledge, namely that dead and unformed faith profits nothing for salvation and is useless for justice. For how can these stand together: that dead faith profits nothing for salvation, and yet that it is one and the same with saving and justifying faith, and is not specifically distinguished from it?
pass_b_english: Rome common teaching that saving justifying faith is not specifically distinct from dead unformed faith seems to clash with their own admission that dead faith profits nothing for salvation or justice.

choices.why: Sets up XLIX resolution of same-species vs uselessness.
